info.name: Betazen Server Panel API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the Betazen Server Panel.

## What is included

1. **Authentication** — JWT login + refresh for both the Platform Owner (WHM) and Vendor (User Panel) surfaces.
2. **Developer · WHM (Platform Owner)** — manage API tokens and outbound webhooks at the super-admin scope; tokens may be pinned to a specific vendor.
3. **Developer · Vendor (User Panel)** — same surface, scoped to the calling vendor's tenant.
4. **Programmatic API** (`/api/v1/external/*`) — token-authenticated endpoints for domain provisioning, SSL, email and Deploy Software linking.

## How to use

1. Click **Import** → select this JSON file.
2. Open **Variables** on the collection and update `base_url`, `owner_email`, `owner_password` (and `vendor_email` / `vendor_password` if you also want to test the vendor surface).
3. Run **Authentication ▸ Login (Platform Owner)** — the test script auto-stores `access_token` and `refresh_token` into the collection variables, so every downstream WHM request authenticates without a manual paste.
4. Run **Developer · WHM ▸ Create API Token** — the test script captures `plaintext_token` into the `api_token` collection variable, so the **Programmatic API** folder requests just work.
5. Run any **Programmatic API** request — they auth using the captured `api_token`.

## Conventions

- All path / id parameters are exposed as `{{collection_variables}}` so you can swap demo values for your real ones in one place.
- Token format is `btz_<env>_<id>_<secret>`; the SECRET half is bcrypt-hashed server-side and shown plaintext exactly once at creation.
- Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>` and delivered with `X-Betazen-Signature: sha256=<hex>` plus `X-Betazen-Timestamp` and `X-Betazen-Delivery` headers.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: JWT-based login. Use these to populate `access_token` for the WHM/Vendor management surfaces. The programmatic `/api/v1/external/*` surface uses an API token instead — see the **Developer** folders.

request.description: Authenticates the platform owner and returns `access_token` (15 min TTL) + `refresh_token` (7 d). The test script stores both into collection variables so every downstream WHM request authenticates automatically.
Authenticates a vendor (vendor_admin role). Stores credentials in `vendor_access_token` so the `Developer · Vendor` folder can drive the User Panel surface in parallel.
Rotates the refresh token and issues a fresh 15-minute access token. Refresh tokens are single-use; the response carries the new pair.

item.name: Developer · WHM (Platform Owner)
item.description:
Manage API tokens and outbound webhooks at the platform-owner scope. Tokens issued here may be pinned to a vendor via `pinned_vendor_id`, immutably scoping every call made with that token to the chosen tenant.

All requests authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` (set by the **Authentication ▸ Login (Platform Owner)** request).

request.description: Returns the catalogue of scopes a token may be granted, grouped by feature: domain / email / ssl / deploy / webhook.
Lists every API token the platform owner has issued, newest first. Secrets are never returned — only `prefix`, `scopes`, `status`, and last-used metadata.

exec: console.log('Stored api_token (shown once) — Programmatic API folder will use it.');

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Acme Provisioning Token",
  "description": "Used by the Acme ops team for domain + mailbox automation",
  "scopes": [
    "domain:read",
    "domain:write",
    "email:read",
    "email:write",
    "email:webmail",
    "ssl:write",
    "deploy:link"
  ],
  "expires_in_days": 90,
  "pinned_vendor_id": "{{vendor_user_id}}",
  "ip_allowlist": ["203.0.113.10", "203.0.113.0/24"]
}

request.description:
Mints a new API token. The plaintext token is in `data.plaintext_token` and shown EXACTLY ONCE — store it before dismissing the response.

- `expires_in_days: 0` means never expire (until revoked).
- `pinned_vendor_id` (owner-only) immutably scopes the token to that vendor's tenant.
- `ip_allowlist` accepts exact IPs and simple CIDRs (`203.0.113.0/24`).
Mints a fresh secret for the same `token_id`. The OLD secret stops working immediately. Response shape mirrors Create — the new plaintext is shown exactly once.
Revokes the token. The bearer string is rejected on the next request; the row is preserved (for audit) with `status=revoked`.
Returns the catalogue of events the panel can fire (domain.created, ssl.issued, email.mailbox.created, deploy.linked, …). Use these keys when subscribing a webhook.
Lists outbound webhook subscriptions visible to the caller. Vendors only see their own; the platform owner sees every subscription.

body.raw:
{
  "url": "https://hooks.example.com/betazen/incoming",
  "description": "Acme integrations \u2014 sync domains + SSL events into our CRM",
  "events": [
    "domain.created",
    "domain.deleted",
    "ssl.issued",
    "ssl.forced",
    "email.mailbox.created",
    "deploy.linked"
  ],
  "active": true
}

request.description: Creates an outbound webhook subscription. `data.plaintext_secret` is the HMAC-SHA256 signing secret and is shown ONCE — your receiver uses it to verify the `X-Betazen-Signature` header.
Updates an existing webhook's active flag, event subscriptions, or description. URL is immutable — to change it, delete and re-create.
Mints a fresh signing secret. The old secret stops verifying immediately; your receiver should be updated with the new one before the next event fires.
Dispatches a synthetic `webhook.test` event so you can confirm the receiver path. The delivery shows up under **List Webhook Deliveries**.
Permanently removes the webhook. Existing delivery rows survive for the 30-day TTL; new dispatches stop immediately.
Recent delivery attempts across every webhook visible to the caller. Each row carries event key, HTTP status, attempt count, error message and timestamps.

item.name: Developer · Vendor (User Panel)
item.description:
Same surface as the WHM Developer folder, but scoped to the vendor's own tenant. Authenticates with `vendor_access_token` (set by **Authentication ▸ Login (Vendor)**).

Vendors cannot pin tokens to other vendors — `pinned_vendor_id` is silently ignored if supplied.

request.description: Lists tokens this vendor owns. Tenant scoping is enforced server-side — vendors never see another vendor's tokens.
Mints a vendor-owned token. Auto-locked to this vendor's tenant via `CallerScope`; cannot exceed the vendor's own RBAC permissions.

item.name: Programmatic API · Domains
item.description:
Token-authenticated programmatic surface. Authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer {{api_token}}` — the plaintext token captured by **Developer · WHM ▸ Create API Token**.

All routes under `/api/v1/external/*` enforce per-route scopes; missing scope returns 403 with the exact scope key required.

request.description: Paginated list of domains visible to the calling token. Required scope: `domain:read`.

Creates a new domain under the linux account specified by `user`. Required scope: `domain:write`.

- For owner-issued tokens with `pinned_vendor_id`, the user must belong to the pinned vendor's tenant.
- For vendor-issued tokens, the user must belong to the calling vendor's tenant.
- The panel sets up nginx, PHP-FPM pool, DNS zone (when delegated), and stamps the WHOIS metadata.

item.name: Programmatic API · Guest links
item.description: Mint one-time, browser-locked guest links for a single domain. Required scope: `guest:create`.

request.description: Returns a one-time login URL (`data.url`) for the domain — redirect the end-user to it. 30-minute window from first open, locked to the first browser. Main domain → Email + DNS; subdomain → Email only. The three limits are optional.

item.name: Programmatic API · Guest session
item.description: The no-login surface a guest link opens (cookie-authed, driven by the User Panel SPA). You normally do NOT call these — you only mint the link (Guest links) and redirect the user. Included here for end-to-end testing: run "Redeem" first (Postman stores the session cookies), then the rest work automatically. Set the {{guest_token}} variable to a freshly minted gst_… token. Every call is hard-scoped to the link's one domain.

request.description: PUBLIC. Opens the link and sets the HttpOnly session cookies on the first call from this client; binds to this browser/agent. Returns { domain, link_type, window_expires_at }.
Returns the domain, link type, email limits, current mailbox count, and the window deadline.
Mailboxes for the session domain.
email may be a bare local part or a full address in the session domain. Quota + send-limit come from the link; 403 once max_mailboxes is reached.
Reset the password for info@<domain>.
Mints a one-click Roundcube SSO URL for info@<domain> — { url, token, expires_in }.
Delete info@<domain>.
Forwarders for the session domain.
source is forced into the session domain.
Main-domain (email_dns) links only; 403 for subdomain (email) links.
Apex @ A/AAAA records are blocked (403). Everything else allowed.
Clears the session cookies.

item.name: Programmatic API · SSL
item.description: Issue and force HTTPS for a domain. Required scope: `ssl:write`.

request.description:
Requests a Let's Encrypt cert for the domain (and any `additional_domains` SAN entries). When `email` is blank, the panel auto-derives `admin@<owning-vendor>` as the ACME contact.

Returns the issued cert metadata (issuer, serial, expires_at). The vhost is upgraded to listen on :443 automatically.
Adds the HTTP→HTTPS 301 redirect to the nginx vhost and stamps `force_ssl=true` on both the cert row and the domain row. Idempotent.
Removes the HTTP→HTTPS redirect — both schemes serve the site again. The certificate stays installed.

item.name: Programmatic API · Email
item.description:
Mailbox + forwarder CRUD plus a single-sign-on link to the Roundcube webmail. Required scopes: `email:read` / `email:write` / `email:webmail`.

The `:domain` path segment scopes every per-domain operation; mailbox addresses can be passed either as the local part (e.g. `john`) or full address (e.g. `john@acme-store.com`).

request.description: Creates the mailbox at `john@{{tenant_domain}}`. Provisions the maildir, writes a SHA512-CRYPT line into `/etc/dovecot/users`, and adds the Postfix virtual-mailbox map entry.
Returns mailbox stats — quota, used MB (live `du`), send-limit, and timestamps. No PII / message content is exposed.

Mints a short-lived, HMAC-signed SSO token. The response includes `url` (e.g. `/webmail/sso.php?token=…`) which can be embedded in your dashboard so end-users open Roundcube without re-entering credentials.
Tears down the maildir, removes the Dovecot user line and Postfix virtual-mailbox entry, then deletes the row.
Creates a forwarder at `sales@{{tenant_domain}}` that fans out to the destination list. `keep_copy: true` retains a copy in the source mailbox if one exists.

item.name: Programmatic API · Deploy Software
item.description:
Link / unlink a registered domain to a Deploy Software service. Required scope: `deploy:link`.

Link (v3.1.117+) DURABLY attaches the domain: it gets its OWN nginx reverse-proxy vhost + its own Let's Encrypt cert, plus a `proxy_service_id` link on the Domain record — so a later service edit, SSL reissue, or server migration can never drop it. The domain must already be registered under Domains and owned by the caller. Unlink detaches it (restores its base vhost) without revoking the cert.

query.description: Optional: substring match against service name OR primary_domain.

request.description:
Required scope: `deploy:read`.

Returns a flat, paginated inventory of every Deploy Software service the calling token can see — across all projects in the tenant. Each row carries the parent project's `project_name`, `project_slug`, and `project_user`, so a consumer can render context ("`web` in project Storefront") without a second round-trip per project.

Tenant scoping mirrors the standard Projects list — vendors only see services in projects belonging to their own tenant. JWT-driven equivalents for in-panel scripting:
- WHM admin: `GET /api/v1/whm/projects/services` (requires `deploy.manage`)
- Vendor:    `GET /api/v1/cpanel/projects/services` (auto-tenant-scoped)

Durably attaches `{{tenant_domain}}` to the service (v3.1.117+): the domain gets its OWN nginx reverse-proxy vhost + its own Let's Encrypt cert, plus a `proxy_service_id` link on the Domain record. Survives service edits, SSL reissue, and server migration. The domain must already be registered and owned by the caller. Response includes the updated service (with `attached_domains`); `ssl_warning` is set if DNS for the domain isn't pointing here yet (it's attached + routing on HTTP, cert issues on a later reissue).

Detaches `{{tenant_domain}}`: clears the `proxy_service_id` link and restores the domain's own base vhost (PHP-FPM, or a placeholder if it's not a registered Domain). The cert is NOT revoked — that would risk downtime and burn an LE rate-limit slot.

variable.description: Panel base URL (no trailing slash). Replace with your deployment, e.g. https://panel.acme.com
Platform-owner login email (vendor_owner role). Set this to your real owner account before running.
Platform-owner password. Replace with the real value before running.
Vendor (vendor_admin role) login email used by the Vendor folder.
ObjectID of the vendor's user row. Used as `pinned_vendor_id` when the platform owner mints a token scoped to that vendor. Look it up via WHM ▸ Vendors or the GET /admin/vendors endpoint.
JWT for the platform owner. Auto-populated by the Login (Platform Owner) test script.
JWT for the vendor surface. Auto-populated by Login (Vendor).
Plaintext btz_<env>_<id>_<secret> token used by the Programmatic API folder. Auto-populated by Developer · WHM ▸ Create API Token.
Plaintext token issued by a vendor for their own automation. Auto-populated by Developer · Vendor ▸ Create Vendor API Token.
HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. Receivers verify X-Betazen-Signature (sha256=<hex>) over <timestamp>.<body>.
Demo domain used by SSL / email / deploy-link requests.
Auto-populated by Programmatic API ▸ Create Domain.
Local part of the mailbox address. Combined with tenant_domain server-side.
Deploy Software project ObjectID. Look it up via WHM ▸ Deploy Software or GET /api/v1/whm/projects.
ProjectService ObjectID — the specific service inside the project that the domain attaches to.
